title: The future of advertising
paragraphs: Imagine a future where our streets are filled with ads 200m tall; where billboards change before our eyes to give us personalised messages; and where companies track our every move as we walk through a city, pinging our phones with special offers as we near their shops.

In fact, all of these forms of advertising are already being tested. Let‘s take the first of these ideas. Back in 1982, science fiction movie Blade Runner envisaged a futuristic cityscape where giant adverts stretched the full height of skyscrapers. And UK company Lightvert are now doing something very similar; with one crucial difference.

Instead of making immense physical adverts, their commercials are beamed straight into consumers’ eyes. They do this by attaching a strip of reflective material to a wall, and then projecting an image onto it. The image then ‘bounces‘ out. You can see it when you walk directly in front of it. It looks huge and suspended in mid- air, but no one else can - you can only see it from one specific spot. Lightvert claims this form of advertising is unobtrusive and that it can “unlock” vast amounts of “high- value advertising real estate”.

But not everyone is sold on the idea of living in a world of endless ads. In Moscow, for example, a new form of advertising targeting motorists has split opinion. Drivers approaching a particular digital billboard in the city are shown adverts for a new kind of Jaguar car, but only if you are driving a different make of vehicle. Sensors in the billboard detect what kind of car you are driving, and send you an ad based on that information.

While this may seem invasive, it’s actually the safety aspect that has concerned some observers. Researchers in Sweden have shown that digital billboards attract our eyes for longer than other kinds. In fact, they distract us for over two seconds, a length of time which studies have proved to be dangerous on the roads.

Finally, we have “proximity marketing”, where shops detect where you are on the high street and send tailored adverts to your phone. Devicescape is one company trialling the use of Wi-Fi as a means of tracking customers. Their technology could work anywhere, whether in “a supermarket, a concert hall, or a bus,” says Owen Geddes from their marketing team. What would customers see? “It could be a discount offer to use in the shop the person is visiting, or a piece of content such as a movie trailer,” says Mr Geddes.

vocabulary.entry: personalised [adj.] /ˈpɜːsənəlaɪzd/ 个性化的 (书面语)
vocabulary.example: The company offers personalised services to customers.
vocabulary.translation: 这家公司为客户提供个性化服务。

vocabulary.entry: pinging [v.] /ˈpɪŋɪŋ/ 发送（信息）；发出响声 (口语；原形: ping)
vocabulary.example: My phone pinged with a new message.
vocabulary.translation: 我的手机叮的一声收到了一条新消息。

vocabulary.entry: beam [v.] /biːm/ 发射（无线电波等）；播送 (书面语)
vocabulary.example: The satellite beamed signals back to Earth.
vocabulary.translation: 卫星向地球发射信号。

vocabulary.entry: bounce [v.] /baʊns/ 反弹；反射
vocabulary.example: The light bounces off the mirror.
vocabulary.translation: 光线从镜子上反射回来。

vocabulary.entry: unobtrusive [adj.] /ˌʌnəbˈtruːsɪv/ 不引人注目的；不显眼的 (书面语)
vocabulary.example: The security cameras are small and unobtrusive.
vocabulary.translation: 这些监控摄像头很小，不引人注目。

vocabulary.entry: sold on [phr.] /səʊld ɒn/ 认同；热衷于 (口语)
vocabulary.example: I’m not sold on the idea of working from home.
vocabulary.translation: 我并不认同在家工作的想法。

vocabulary.entry: split opinion [phr.] /splɪt əˈpɪnjən/ 引发意见分歧
vocabulary.example: The new policy split opinion among voters.
vocabulary.translation: 这项新政策在选民中引发了意见分歧。

vocabulary.entry: invasive [adj.] /ɪnˈveɪsɪv/ 侵入性的；侵扰的
vocabulary.example: Some people find targeted ads invasive.
vocabulary.translation: 有些人觉得定向广告具有侵扰性。

vocabulary.entry: distract [v.] /dɪˈstrækt/ 使分心；使分散注意力
vocabulary.example: The noise distracted me from my work.
vocabulary.translation: 噪音使我无法专心工作。

vocabulary.entry: proximity marketing [n.] /prɒkˈsɪməti ˌmɑːkɪtɪŋ/ 近距离营销 (专业术语)
vocabulary.example: Proximity marketing sends offers to customers‘ phones when they are near a store.
vocabulary.translation: 当顾客靠近商店时，近距离营销会向他们的手机发送优惠信息。

vocabulary.entry: tailored [adj.] /ˈteɪləd/ 定制的；专门设计的 (书面语)
vocabulary.example: The course provides tailored training for each student.
vocabulary.translation: 这门课程为每个学生提供量身定制的培训。

vocabulary.entry: envisage [v.] /ɪnˈvɪzɪdʒ/ 设想；想象 (书面语)
vocabulary.example: It is difficult to envisage life without electricity.
vocabulary.translation: 很难想象没有电的生活。

vocabulary.entry: futuristic [adj.] /ˌfjuːtʃəˈrɪstɪk/ 未来派的；有未来感的
vocabulary.example: The building has a futuristic design.
vocabulary.translation: 这座建筑有未来派的设计。

vocabulary.entry: skyscraper [n.] /ˈskaɪskreɪpə/ 摩天大楼
vocabulary.example: The city skyline is dominated by skyscrapers.
vocabulary.translation: 这座城市的天际线以摩天大楼为主。

vocabulary.entry: immense [adj.] /ɪˈmens/ 巨大的；广大的
vocabulary.example: The project requires immense effort.
vocabulary.translation: 这个项目需要巨大的努力。

vocabulary.entry: commercials [n. pl.] /kəˈmɜːʃəlz/ 商业广告 (口语；单数: commercial)
vocabulary.example: I hate watching commercials on TV.
vocabulary.translation: 我讨厌看电视上的广告。

vocabulary.entry: reflective [adj.] /rɪˈflektɪv/ 反射的；反光的
vocabulary.example: The road signs are made of reflective material.
vocabulary.translation: 道路标志是用反光材料制作的。

vocabulary.entry: projecting [v.] /prəˈdʒektɪŋ/ 投射；投影 (原形: project)
vocabulary.example: The teacher is projecting the image onto the screen.
vocabulary.translation: 老师正在把图像投射到屏幕上。

vocabulary.entry: suspended [adj.] /səˈspendɪd/ 悬浮的；暂停的
vocabulary.example: The lights were suspended from the ceiling.
vocabulary.translation: 灯悬挂在天花板上。

vocabulary.entry: sensors [n. pl.] /ˈsensəz/ 传感器 (专业词汇；单数: sensor)
vocabulary.example: The robot uses sensors to detect obstacles.
vocabulary.translation: 机器人使用传感器探测障碍物。

vocabulary.entry: motorist [n.] /ˈməʊtərɪst/ 驾驶汽车的人；驾车者
vocabulary.example: The road is closed, so motorists should find an alternative route.
vocabulary.translation: 这条路封闭了，驾车者应该寻找替代路线。

vocabulary.entry: make of [n.] /meɪk əv/ 品牌；型号
vocabulary.example: What make of car do you drive?
vocabulary.translation: 你开的是什么牌子的车？

vocabulary.entry: real estate [n.] /ˈrɪəl ɪˌsteɪt/ 不动产；房地产 (此处比喻广告空间)
vocabulary.example: The company invested in commercial real estate.
vocabulary.translation: 这家公司投资了商业房地产。

vocabulary.entry: high street [n.] /ˈhaɪ striːt/ 商业街 (英式英语)
vocabulary.example: There are many shops on the high street.
vocabulary.translation: 商业街上有很多商店。

vocabulary.entry: trailer [n.] /ˈtreɪlə/ 预告片
vocabulary.example: The movie trailer was released last week.
vocabulary.translation: 这部电影的预告片上周发布了。

sentences.english: In fact, all of these forms of advertising are already being tested.
sentences.chinese: 事实上，所有这些形式的广告都已经在测试中了。

sentences.chinese: 我们先来看看第一个设想。

sentences.chinese: 英国公司Lightvert现在也在做类似的事情，不过有一个关键的区别。

sentences.english: Instead of making immense physical adverts, their commercials are beamed straight into consumers’ eyes.
sentences.chinese: 他们没有制作巨大的实体广告，而是将广告直接投射到消费者的眼睛里。

sentences.english: They do this by attaching a strip of reflective material to a wall, and then projecting an image onto it.
sentences.chinese: 他们通过在墙上贴一条反光材料，然后将图像投射到上面来实现这一点的。

sentences.chinese: 它看起来巨大且悬浮在半空中，但其他人看不到——只有在一个特定的位置才能看到。

sentences.chinese: Lightvert公司声称这种形式的广告不引人注目，并且能够“解锁”大量的“高价值广告不动产”。

sentences.chinese: 但并不是每个人都赞同生活在一个充斥着无尽广告的世界里。

sentences.chinese: 例如，在莫斯科，一种针对司机的的新型广告引发了意见分歧。

sentences.english: Drivers approaching a particular digital billboard in the city are shown adverts for a new kind of Jaguar car, but only if you are driving a different make of vehicle.
sentences.chinese: 当驾驶员接近城市中某个特定的数字广告牌时，会看到一个新型捷豹汽车的广告，但前提是你驾驶的是其他品牌的车辆。

sentences.english: Sensors in the billboard detect what kind of car you are driving, and send you an ad based on that information.
sentences.chinese: 广告牌中的传感器会检测你驾驶的汽车类型，并根据该信息向你发送广告。

sentences.chinese: 瑞典的研究人员已经表明，数字广告牌吸引我们目光的时间比其他类型的广告牌更长。

sentences.chinese: 事实上，它们会让我们在道路上分心超过两秒钟，而研究已经证明，这个时长是很危险的。
